papers.title: Boosting the quality factor of Tamm structures to millions by quantum inspired classical annealer with factorization machine
papers.abstract: The Tamm structures show high quality (Q) factor property with simple photonic Bragg reflectors composed of alternative high/low refractive index layers and metal reflectors. However, the Q-factor of Tamm structures is inherently limited by the periodic constraints and fixed thicknesses of the Bragg reflector pairs. Removing periodic constraints and adopting aperiodic designs can lead to significantly higher Q-factors. Nevertheless, to fully exploit the potential of Tamm structures, it is essential to thoroughly explore the extensive search space introduced by these aperiodic designs. Herein, we introduce a novel approach that utilizes the quantum-inspired classical annealer combined with a factorization machine to facilitate the design of photonic Bragg reflectors with the aim of achieving ultrahigh Q-factor properties. Our investigation begins by establishing the effectiveness of global optimization in a 15-bit problem setting, showcasing a remarkable efficiency improvement of nearly one order of magnitude compared to random search strategies. Subsequently, we expand our analysis to a 20-bit problem, demonstrating comparable efficiency to state-of-the-art Bayesian optimization methods. Moreover, the proposed method proves its capability in handling extremely large search spaces, exemplified by a 40-bit problem, where we successfully uncover a Tamm structure design exhibiting an extraordinary ultrahigh Q-factor surpassing millions. The designed aperiodic Tamm structure exhibits exceptional high localization and enhancement of electric field, and the power loss is concentrated in the low loss dielectric layer. Hence, the decay rate of power dissipation significantly decreases and light-matter interaction time increases, resulting in ultrahigh Q-factor.

summary_en.motivation: To achieve ultrahigh Q-factors in Tamm structures by exploring aperiodic designs without periodic constraints.
summary_en.method: A quantum-inspired classical annealer combined with a factorization machine is used to optimize Bragg reflector thicknesses.
summary_en.result: A Tamm structure with Q-factor exceeding millions is discovered in a 40-bit optimization problem.
summary_en.validation: The optimization efficiency is validated against random search and Bayesian optimization benchmarks.

papers.title: No difference in early functional outcome between the direct anterior approach and posterior approach in patients following total hip arthroplasty
papers.abstract: Background: Objective and subjective outcomes in the direct anterior approach (DAA) and posterior approach (PA) in total hip arthroplasty (THA) were assessed in this study, using the Oxford Hip Score (OHS) as primary outcome. Pain, 3 objective performance-based tests, surgical time, blood loss and length of stay were assessed as secondary outcomes. Methods: Patients with primary end-stage osteoarthritis were prospectively enrolled by shared decision making for the DAA (32 patients) or PA (26 patients). Baseline data were collected preoperatively and outcomes postoperatively at 2-, 6-, 9- and 12-month follow-up. Results: There is no significant difference (p < 0.05) between the DAA and PA on primary outcome (OHS). There was a main effect of time which indicated an increase of OHS over time independent of group (p < 0.01). Conclusions: In the current study, no significant differences in postoperative functional outcome were found between DAA and PA in all follow-up moments.

summary_zh.motivation: 比较直接前入路与后入路在全髋关节置换术后的早期功能结果。
summary_zh.method: 前瞻性纳入58例患者，分别采用DAA或PA，术后随访12个月。
summary_zh.result: 两组在Oxford髋关节评分上无显著差异，功能随时间改善。
summary_zh.validation: 临床随访数据统计分析。

summary_en.motivation: To compare early functional outcomes between the direct anterior approach and posterior approach in total hip arthroplasty.
summary_en.method: A prospective cohort study enrolled 58 patients who underwent THA via DAA or PA with follow-up at 2, 6, 9, and 12 months.
summary_en.result: No significant difference in Oxford Hip Score between groups; scores improved over time independently of approach.
summary_en.validation: Statistical analysis of clinical follow-up data with performance-based tests.
